overview: Gonorrhoea is a common sexually transmitted infection caused by a bacteria. It usually spreads through vaginal, oral or anal sex. Gonorrhoea is treatable and curable with antibiotics. Most cases of gonorrhoea can be prevented with regular and correct condom use.
symptoms: white, yellow or greenish discharge from the penis
vaginal bleeding between periods or during sexual intercourse
diagnosis: Sexual history taking and risk assessment
Swabs from genital and other sites (anus, throat, conjunctiva)
treatment: Wait 7 days after taking the medicine before having sex
Notify sexual partner(s) to get tested or treated
risk_factors: Men who have sex with men
Adolescents and young people in high burden countries
complications: Infection in multiple organs of the body (skin, heart, joints and meninges)
key_facts: 82.4 million new infections among adults globally in 2020
Most women with gonorrhoea do not have symptoms
Antimicrobial resistance to gonorrhoea is a serious and growing problem
Gonorrhoea can be passed from a pregnant mother to her baby
Gonococcal infection increases the risk of getting and spreading HIV
